newsitem.title: JAPAN: China Daqing crude volume to Japan seen off in '97.
newsitem.headline: China Daqing crude volume to Japan seen off in '97.

text.p: China's crude oil allocation to Japan is expected to fall short of the 8.5 million tonnes lifted in 1996, due to rising domestic demand in China, Japanese traders said on Tuesday.

Traders declined to speculate on what the volume for 1997 would be, but they said it was likely to be within the six to eight million tonne amount that China agreed to lift to Japan under a five-year contract beginning in 1996.
"I don't know how much it will be...but the contract was for between six to eight million tonnes," one trader said, implying that next year's allocation would fall within that range.
China agreed to supply Japan with 8.5 million tonnes in 1996, more than the amount stipulated in the five-year contract, at the request of Japanese companies, traders said.

When a Japanese delegation visited Beijing in October to negotiate the contract for 1997, the Japanese companies asked for a volume similar to this year's, a source familiar with the negotiations said.

He added, however, that while the Chinese did not give an immediate response to the request, a Chinese official told the delegation he was "sure that Japan understands the domestic situation in China."

The Chinese representatives said they would give their response at the end of January, a delay from their usual practice of replying in December, the trader added. The Chinese officials did not give a specific reason for the delay.
China reviews its Daqing export volume every five years.
Most Daqing crude exported to Japan is lifted on a term basis.
